6. HOW A CHANGE REACHES YOUR REPO
Each task (one small piece of work with its own branch) gets its own branch, named feature/ and
the task number (for example feature/t-001), cut from the newest main. The gates run on the
branch and on a trial merge with the newest main. You approve the exact commit. Then I push that
branch and open a pull request on GitHub. Your team reviews and merges as usual; their hooks and
CI decide. Your repo will show this of me; tell me any line to change:
- Commit identity: Shop Bot <bot@shop.example> (you chose it)
- Pull request footer: on, the body says it was made with an agent assistant (you chose it)
- Branch prefix: feature/ (your repo's own rule) [6]

7. HOW MUCH I DO ALONE: L2

at a time and show it to you before the next. Why L2: others share this repo. Say "raise the
